title: Canonical normalized classical Weil realization data
statement: For the finite-field datum and geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-punctual-weights], a separated finite-type scheme $Y_0$, a coefficient prime $\ell\ne p$ and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, define the normalized classical lisse Weil realization datum on $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. It consists of the normalized adic model data [def-zl-adic-lisse-calculus-models], a functor from classical lisse algebraic-coefficient sheaves [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves] to the sf common-stage constructible category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], its identification with that model realization (realization into [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category] followed by the model comparison), membership in the actual sf common-stage constructible heart [def-weil-constructible-heart], and its comparison with the sf common-stage Frobenius pullback of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. At EVERY finite coefficient subfield the comparison must be pinned to [def-real-lisse-realization-data], [def-real-lisse-pullback-normalization] at geometric Frobenius and [def-per-lisse-completed-system-data] for the same map and identity coefficient map: fix the coefficient isomorphism pointwise by the Shrink equivalence, a natural scalar-linear underlying sheaf comparison, and the square equating the ordinary module pullback unit followed by the normalized lisse comparison to the completed rational pullback unit followed by its normalized comparison. At every finite reduction the completed etale unit followed by the inverse raw integral identification equals the canonical adjunction unit into literal automorphism reindexing [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]. Finally identify the actual raw pullback objects with the classical pullback objects, and require the common-stage Frobenius comparison to equal the transported finite comparison through one natural finite-stage realization isomorphism. The remaining endpoint identifications are equality transports, not free isomorphisms. Use the classical Weil category of [def-wf-fundamental-representation]. The associated Weil functor transports BOTH the Weil map and its inverse along this pinned comparison. These are data and defining compatibility conditions, not an existence theorem.
